ui.battle.examineHint: Interrogate the claim. It is free.
ui.battle.refuteHint: Build a syllogism that answers it.
ui.battle.claimHint: Assert a conclusion on its own.
ui.battle.embraceHint: Let it stand. They will take that.
ui.battle.duplicate: You already have that one in the argument.
ui.battle.readout.parts: A syllogism has three parts: a major premise, a minor premise, a conclusion.
ui.battle.readout.minor: Now the minor premise. It must carry the middle term and the subject of the conclusion.
ui.battle.readout.middleTerm: The middle term has to turn up in both premises and nowhere in the conclusion.
ui.battle.readout.figure1: the middle term is the subject of the major and the predicate of the minor
ui.battle.readout.figure2: the middle term is the predicate in both premises
ui.battle.readout.figure3: the middle term is the subject in both premises
ui.battle.readout.figure4: the middle term is the predicate of the major and the subject of the minor
ui.logic.holds: That is {mood} in figure {figure}: {name}. It holds.
ui.logic.invalidMood: That is {mood} in figure {figure}, and that mood does not hold.
ui.logic.notSyllogism: That is not a syllogism. The middle term has to turn up in both premises and nowhere in the conclusion.
ui.logic.conclusionNotSP: The conclusion has to be about the subject and the predicate of the whole argument, and nothing else.
ui.logic.termsSwapped: The premises do not line up. The major premise is about the middle term and the predicate, and the minor premise is about the subject and the middle term.
